facts.text: UnderwaterCurrentROSPlugin reads the optional namespace SDF element and creates its ROS node handle from it.
UnderwaterCurrentROSPlugin advertises a geometry_msgs/TwistStamped flow velocity on the configured currentVelocityTopic.
UnderwaterCurrentPlugin defaults the flow topic name to current_velocity when the SDF topic element is absent.
UnderwaterCurrentROSPlugin advertises the relative services set_current_velocity, set_current_horz_angle and set_current_vert_angle.
The plugin header includes geometry_msgs/TwistStamped, uuv_world_ros_plugins_msgs/SetCurrentVelocity and uuv_world_ros_plugins_msgs/SetCurrentDirection.
UpdateCurrentVelocity calls SetMean on the velocity, horizontal-angle and vertical-angle models and sets success true only when all three calls succeed.
GaussMarkovProcess::SetMean returns false when the requested mean is outside the model's configured minimum and maximum.
GaussMarkovProcess::Reset sets the process state var to mean, and SetMean calls Reset after storing an in-range mean.
GaussMarkovProcess::Update scales var by (1 - step * mu), adds noiseAmp times a uniform random number in [-0.5, 0.5] and clamps var to the configured min and max.
The velocity model range is read from the constant_current SDF block; it is deployment configuration.
The horizontal-angle model range is read from the constant_current SDF block; it is deployment configuration.
The vertical-angle model range is read from the constant_current SDF block; it is deployment configuration.
The shipped auv_underwater_world.world configures the current velocity range as 0 to 5 m/s and the angle ranges as -3.141592653589793238 to 3.141592653589793238 rad under the hydrodynamics namespace.
OnUpdateCurrentVel publishes the current flow vector in the /world frame when the ROS publish period has elapsed.
The ROS plugin constructor sets rosPublishPeriod to 0.05 s.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies; no world update, Gauss-Markov process, physics or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS current-environment contract stand-in (no world or physics)
gaps: the fake answers the declared services and flow topic and runs no ROS node, rosbridge, Gazebo world, Gauss-Markov process, ocean current field, physics or vehicle dynamics
the real plugin updates the current models on world updates and publishes the flow vector at a 0.05 s period; the fake replies immediately with a canned vector
the fake maps a commanded mean directly to its flow vector; the real current is the Gauss-Markov process output and may differ from the mean
the zero-current request requires all three configured model ranges to include zero; otherwise the service returns success false and the e-stop fails with the latch held

upstream UpdateCurrentVelocity calls SetMean on the velocity, horizontal and vertical models in that order and stops at the first refusal, so a refused request can leave an earlier mean changed; the fake checks all three ranges before changing any mean
after SetMean the Gauss-Markov update adds noiseAmp noise and clamps to the configured range; the fake has no noise, so its zero-current flow is exactly zero
while Gazebo is paused the plugin publishes no flow sample (it publishes on world updates), so the flow read is refused NOT_READY; the fake always answers
the package exposes the current setters, the flow observation and the zero-current safe state; the model getter/setter services are out of scope
the endpoint prefix /hydrodynamics is the namespace in the shipped world; the operator must configure or remap the actual namespace
no live ROS graph, Gazebo world or hardware run was performed; the evidence is contract_checked only

safe_state.description: The fixed set_current_velocity request sets the velocity, horizontal-angle and vertical-angle model means to zero, and SetMean resets each process state to its mean, so the simulated flow is zero from the next world update while the velocity model's noiseAmp is zero (with noise it varies about zero within the configured range). It does not stop the vehicle or the Gazebo world. It is refused when any of the three configured ranges excludes zero; the velocity mean may then already be zero.
